subject: Dedicated capacity traffic scan — CarbonAI deal
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina@carbonai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 21:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity traffic scan — quick data request

Hi Nina,

Thanks again for the time last week. To get us moving on a tight timeline, can you send a short telemetry export (CSV) that shows: avg concurrent sessions by hour (last 30 days), percentile token lengths for prompt and response (p50/p95/p99), percent of sessions using long-context summarization (>8k tokens), and any nightly batch/async embedding jobs that run between 22:00-03:00 local time?

If you already have a weekly breakdown, that’s fine — we mainly need the burst shape (minute-level preferred for peak days), example payload sizes, and a sense of KV cache hit rates if you have them. Attaching a simple template (traffic-export-sample.csv) that our sizing workbook expects.

Target constraints we should assume for sizing: 200ms p95 generation latency for interactive chat, 1.5M prompts/month, and a cost target (infrastructure-only) of ~$0.002/token on average. If any of those are unrealistic for your workload, flag it.

Next steps: if you can drop the CSV and any notes by EOD Thu (19 Jul), Naomi will run a quick sizing and we’ll propose a minimal reserved pool plus autoscale buffer. Also cc’d Ben from sales to coordinate procurement timing.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0118

Attachments: traffic-export-sample.csv (CSV template)
From: Nina Patel <nina@carbonai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Gomez <agomez@carbonai.com>, procurement@carbonai.com
Date: Tue, 17 Jul 2028 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity traffic scan — quick data request

Camila —

Thanks for the clear template. I’m attaching the CSV with 30 days of anonymized minute-level session starts and token counts, plus a short notes file. Quick answers inline:
- Peak concurrent (observed): ~1,120 simultaneous sessions (two peaks between 10:30–11:15 and 14:45–15:30 PT on weekdays).
- Token lengths: prompt p50=85 / p95=1,200 / p99=3,400; response p50=120 / p95=1,800 / p99=4,600.
- Long-context summarization: about 9% of sessions hit >8k prompt tokens; these are mostly nightly ingest summaries and enterprise customers.
- KV cache: not currently instrumented per-se; cache-like behavior exists in an application layer we can export if helpful.
- Nightly batch: yes — a set of async jobs between 23:00–02:30 PT (~2.2M tokens total per night).

We’re also running an embeddings pipeline (async) that spikes after data ingestion windows; those requests are usually queued and tolerant of higher latency. I’m attaching the CSV: traffic-export-sample.csv and a short note: carbonai-telemetry-notes.txt.

Happy to jump on a call Thu morning if that helps.

—Nina
Nina Patel
Infrastructure Lead, CarbonAI
nina@carbonai.com

Attachments: traffic-export-sample.csv (filled), carbonai-telemetry-notes.txt
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Nina Patel <nina@carbonai.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity traffic scan — quick data request

Thanks Nina — appreciate the quick turnaround. Camila / Naomi, high level thoughts before the SE analysis:
- The two daily interactive peaks + nightly large async jobs mean we should plan a mixed pool: reserved GPU capacity sized for typical day peaks, with burst autoscale for the nightly ingest and occasional marketing-driven spikes.
- Because ~9% are >8k, we must ensure enough memory headroom (or fallback model) for long-context summarization. Consider a smaller family for short-chat traffic to reduce cost.
- Procurement: procurement@carbonai.com is looped for potential 12-month reserved commit. Ben will coordinate discounting based on commit size.

Naomi — can you take the CSV and produce a quick SKU mix (A100xlarge vs H100-like, and an alternate quantized T4-style plan for cost-sensitive paths)? If possible, include queueing headroom and a recommended autoscale policy (min reserved, burst max), plus an estimate of effective $/token.

If we can get a preliminary by Thu EOD (19 Jul), we’ll share a slide with CarbonAI and lock a 30-min call.

—Ben
VP, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Nina Patel <nina@carbonai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Preliminary sizing & recommendations — CarbonAI (CARB-2028-321)

Hi all — I ran the attached quick workbook (prelim-sizing.xlsx) against the CSV. Key findings and recommended plan below — this is conservative, assumes 70% KV cache hit for short-chat after app-level warmups (we should validate):

Summary numbers (baseline):
- Typical weekday daytime peak (10:30–11:15): 1,120 concurrent 
- Observed 99th token lengths drive memory requirements for ~9% of sessions (>8k tokens).
- Nightly async ingest: ~2.2M tokens across a 3.5h window — bandwidth-heavy but latency-tolerant.

Recommended fleet mix (reserved + burst):
- Reserved baseline: 12 x H100-equivalent nodes (high-memory configuration) reserved for long-context sessions and steady interactive load.
- Short-chat optimized tier (reserved): 6 x A100-equivalent nodes (cost/perf sweet spot) to handle the bulk of low-context sessions.
- Burst/autoscale pool (on-demand): up to 10 additional smaller instances (quantized) for embedding and batch spikes.

Autoscale / routing policy suggestions:
- Route by session type: long-context sessions -> H100-pool; short-chat -> A100-pool; async embeddings -> burst pool (queued).
- Min-reserved: keep 85% of weekday sustained baseline covered by reserved pool; allow autoscale to cover 15–25% of peak and nightly batch windows.

Latency / cost estimate (very rough):
- Interactive p95 target 200ms: achievable for short-chat on A100 tier with batching and prefix caching; long-context p95 will be higher — estimate 400–700ms depending on KV cache effectiveness.
- Effective infra cost estimate: $0.0016–$0.0024 per token depending on quantization and real cache hit rates — we used conservative kernel/IO assumptions.

Open items / telemetry gaps to validate:
1) Actual KV cache hit-rate after app warmup (we assumed 70%).
2) Session stickiness: do users repeatedly hit same session id (improves cache).
3) Minute-level burst characteristics for top 5 marketing days (we have day-level but minute detail improves autoscale sizing).
4) Failure SLOs and acceptable queueing delays for embeddings.

Attachments included: prelim-sizing.xlsx, kv-cache-modeling.ipynb, and a draft SLA (SLA-draft-CarbonAI.pdf) that maps to the proposed reserved pool.

Proposed next steps:
- Quick 30-min call to walk the deck and agree on reserved commit size and discount banding (I can demo the routing policy in the console).
- Nina: if you can validate KV cache hit-rate and send minute-level burst windows for the two top days, I’ll update numbers and produce a final recommended reserved quantity.

Availability: I have slots Thu 19 Jul 15:00–16:00 PT or Fri 20 Jul 09:00–10:00 PT. Camila / Ben — what works for the CarbonAI team?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Attachments: prelim-sizing.xlsx, kv-cache-modeling.ipynb, SLA-draft-CarbonAI.pdf

I’ve tentatively scheduled a 30-min review for Thu 19 Jul 15:30 PT (calendar invite sent) to walk through the sizing and next steps. If that time doesn’t work for CarbonAI, please propose one alternate.
